title: Customer Care Guide: Disruption Months on Extension of Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers
content:
**Compensation term.** The extension term of a credit of Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers counts disruption months. These count the disruption records with a controllable cause recorded on the customer's tickets under Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand in the last 12 calendar months:

- **2 months** for at least 2 such records;
- **1 month** for exactly one;
- **none** for none.

**Window.** An extension-term window of the last so many calendar months holds the entries dated fewer than that many whole calendar months before the request date, so it rolls back from that date and is not a count of completed calendar months.

**Records counted.** Disruption records on any of the customer's tickets whose cause is classified controllable, recorded inside the window. Records with an uncontrollable cause are not counted.

## Records and months

| Controllable-cause disruption records in the last 12 calendar months | Disruption months |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | 2 |
| exactly 1 | 1 |
| none | none |

## Hypothetical case (request dated 1 July 2026)

The customer's tickets carry controllable disruption records dated 2 July 2025 and 18 March 2026, and an uncontrollable one dated 4 May 2026. The 2 July 2025 record is 11 whole calendar months back and counts. The uncontrollable record does not count. Two records count, so the disruption months are 2. Had the first record been dated 1 July 2025, it would be 12 whole calendar months back and outside the window, and the disruption months would be 1.
